# Inference, serving and cost

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/inference-economics.md) · ← [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md)

Serving models at scale: prefill and decode, batching, caching, quantisation, latency metrics and the levers that move cost.

## Both tracks

- **Distinguish time to first token, time per output token, inter-token latency and throughput when comparing serving systems.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Microsoft](../companies/microsoft.md) †, [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether user-visible delay is separated from aggregate capacity.
- **How would you benchmark vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM and a custom runtime for a specific workload?**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether a reproducible workload drives the choice instead of a generic ranking.
- **You are asked to reduce serving cost by an order of magnitude. Rank the levers and explain how you would test whether that target is achievable.**
  - Applied scenario · Asked at: [Amazon](../companies/amazon.md) †, [Microsoft](../companies/microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether savings are measured under explicit quality and latency constraints.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Measure cost per successful task at the required quality and SLO.
    - Compare smaller models, shorter contexts, reuse, batching and precision changes.
    - Benchmark each change and check whether the combined savings actually reach the target.
  - Read: [Optimizing inference](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/llm_optims) (Hugging Face Transformers docs) · [Site Reliability Engineering](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/) (Google)

## AI Engineering

- **Contrast prefill with autoregressive decode and explain when compute or memory bandwidth becomes the bottleneck.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether bottlenecks are conditioned on workload and batch size.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Prefill processes prompt positions in parallel; decode advances autoregressively.
    - Small-batch decode often reads weights with limited arithmetic reuse.
    - Profile sequence lengths and batching before declaring either phase compute- or bandwidth-bound.
  - Read: [Optimizing inference](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/llm_optims) (Hugging Face Transformers docs)
- **Explain iteration-level batching and how requests enter and leave a running inference batch.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †
  - Tests: Whether scheduling is connected to utilisation, fairness and waiting time.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Admit new sequences at iteration boundaries and remove completed ones.
    - Enforce token and KV-memory budgets rather than request count alone.
    - Measure queueing and starvation alongside throughput.
  - Read: [Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180) (Kwon et al., arXiv)
- **How does paging the KV cache reduce waste, and what remains for the scheduler to solve?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether memory management is distinguished from request scheduling.
- **Explain exact speculative decoding, its acceptance step and workloads where the draft model adds overhead instead of speed.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether speedup is explained without promising a universal quality or latency benefit.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - A smaller model proposes several tokens for parallel target verification.
    - Describe acceptance and correction sampling that preserve the target distribution.
    - Evaluate acceptance rate, draft cost and available parallel compute.
  - Read: [Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192) (Leviathan et al., arXiv)
- **What makes a prompt prefix reusable, and which changes invalidate or reduce the value of a prefix cache?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether exact reuse, cache lifetime and tenant isolation are considered.
- **Compare floating-point and integer serving formats down to four bits; how would you validate an acceptable reduction in precision?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether memory savings are checked against quality, kernels and hardware support.
- **Compare tensor, pipeline, data, sequence and expert parallelism for a large model deployment.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Amazon](../companies/amazon.md) †, [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) †, [Meta](../companies/meta.md) †
  - Tests: Whether communication patterns and memory limits determine the choice.
- **Estimate a serving memory budget for a 70-billion-parameter model, explicitly choosing precision, context and concurrency assumptions.**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether weights, cache and runtime headroom are all budgeted.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Weight storage is parameter count times bytes per parameter, before quantisation metadata.
    - Add architecture-specific KV storage for the chosen concurrent sequences.
    - Reserve activations, workspace and allocator headroom; state any sharding assumptions.
  - Read: [Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180) (Kwon et al., arXiv)
- **Build a roofline estimate for single-request decoding of a 70B model on an H100; check first whether the chosen representation fits.**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether bandwidth, capacity and achievable utilisation constrain the estimate.
- **After a deployment, p99 latency doubles although model weights are unchanged. How do you isolate the cause?**
  - Applied scenario · Asked at: [Amazon](../companies/amazon.md) †, [Databricks](../companies/databricks.md) †, [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †, [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether diagnosis separates queueing, scheduling, dependencies and traffic changes.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Compare traffic mix, queue time and per-stage latency before and after release.
    - Inspect cache hit rates, batching, dependency tails and resource saturation.
    - Reproduce one hypothesis at a time and use a rollback or canary to verify causality.
  - Read: [The Tail at Scale](https://research.google/pubs/the-tail-at-scale/) (Dean and Barroso, Google Research)
- **Why can splitting prefill into chunks help mixed prompt and decode traffic, and what trade-off does chunk size introduce?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether throughput and decode stalls are considered together.
- **When would you separate prefill and decode onto different workers, and how would you price the KV transfer overhead?**
  - System design
  - Tests: Whether independent scaling is weighed against transport and operational complexity.
